Solid oxide electrolyzers are the least mature of the three electrolyzer types described, but there have been several demonstration projects using this electrolyzer type, and several more projects are planned before 2030. Bloom Energy is one of the primary manufacturers of solid oxide electrolyzers as of 2025 (IEA 2025). Estimates of hydrogen losses from conventional gaseous hydrogen production vary but are usually around 1%–4% or less, with electrolysis pathways noted as having higher losses than fossil-based pathways (Esquivel-Elizondo et al. 2023). Hydrogen losses at this step can be minimized by recombining vented or purged hydrogen to form water. Additional hydrogen production methods include biomass gasification, methane pyrolysis, anion-exchange membrane electrolysis, and geologic hydrogen. None of these production techniques are deployed at large scale as of 2025, but there is reason to believe this could change in the future. As noted, gasification is a mature technology that is a major hydrogen production method in China, where coal is the feedstock. However, gasification using biomass is less common, largely due to the high cost of the biomass feedstock, additional processing steps, and equipment needed to acquire high-purity hydrogen output (Lewis et al. 2022; DOE n.d.-g). A key reason to believe biomass gasification installations could accelerate in the future is the renewable nature of the production process. If CCS infrastructure is connected to biomass gasification plants, the production process can even be a net sink for CO on a life cycle basis (Puig-Samper et al. 2024; 2 Lundgren et al. 2025). In the absence of policy support, improvements in the biomass collection and processing steps—as well as biomass gasification technology advancements—would be needed to make this production process more cost-competitive with alternatives. 47 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Another promising hydrogen production pathway is methane pyrolysis. In this production pathway, methane (CH ) is directly converted into hydrogen and carbon through high- 4 temperature decomposition. This reaction occurs in the absence of oxygen such that the byproduct is carbon instead of CO . Hence, there are zero direct pollutants from methane 2 pyrolysis. The carbon black generated during the hydrogen production process may even have value on the market, as carbon is typically used in making plastics, car tires, and batteries (Willige 2021). Several startups are looking to develop methane pyrolysis technology including Monolith Inc. (plasma pyrolysis), Graphitic Energy (formerly C-Zero; catalytic molten media pyrolysis), and Modern Hydrogen (thermal pyrolysis) (Graphitic Energy n.d.; Modern Hydrogen n.d.; Monolith n.d.). Anion-exchange membrane electrolyzers are also being developed by several startups including Enapter, Evoloh, and Power to Hydrogen (P2H2) (Enapter n.d.; Evoloh n.d.; Power to Hydrogen n.d.). These electrolyzers are described as a hybrid between alkaline and PEM electrolyzers, achieving ramping rates similar to PEM electrolyzers to match renewable electricity generation profiles, but with no critical material requirement, similar to alkaline electrolyzers.
